items.jp: 朝は味噌の汁を飲みます
items.kana: あさわみそのしるをのみます

structure_explanation.en: は marks 朝 ('morning') as the topic (the setting being talked about), の links 味噌 ('miso') to 汁 ('broth/soup'), forming 'miso soup', and を marks that soup as the object of 飲む ('to drink/to have'). 飲みます is the polite present/habitual form. The vocabulary focus is 味噌 ('miso'). In Japanese, soup is 'drunk' (飲む), which is why we use 'to have' in English.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: は marca 朝 ('manhã') como o tópico (o cenário sobre o qual se fala), の liga 味噌 ('missô') a 汁 ('caldo/sopa'), formando 'sopa de missô', e を marca essa sopa como objeto de 飲む ('beber/tomar'). 飲みます é a forma polida no presente/habitual. O foco do vocabulário é 味噌 ('missô'). Em japonês, sopa se 'bebe' (飲む), por isso usamos 'tomar' em pt-BR.

translation_literal.en: As for the morning (は), miso (の) soup (を), I drink (polite form).
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto à manhã (は), de missô (の) o caldo/sopa (を), tomo (forma polida).

translation.en: In the morning I have miso soup.
translation.pt-BR: De manhã eu tomo sopa de missô.

conjugation_note.en: connective stem 飲み of 飲む, linked to ます
conjugation_note.pt-BR: raiz conetiva 飲み de 飲む, ligada a ます

conjugation_note.en: ます; 飲みます = polite present/habitual
conjugation_note.pt-BR: ます; 飲みます = presente/habitual polido

findings.issue: Generated JP is unnatural: miso soup is the fixed compound 味噌汁 (みそしる); natives do not say 味噌の汁 for the dish. The sentence teaches a phrase no native uses (the expl even builds the の-linking lesson on it). Fixing requires updating kana/romaji/tokens/expl too.
findings.current: 朝は味噌の汁を飲みます
findings.proposed: 朝は味噌汁を飲みます

items.jp: 背がいたいので病院に行く
items.kana: せがいたいのでびょういんにいく

structure_explanation.en: The sentence chains a cause and a consequence using ので ('because/since'). The first part 背がいたい ('my back hurts') is the reason; the second 病院に行く ('I am going to the hospital') is the result. The parser split ので into の + で, but it functions as a single unit: the causal conjunction ので, which links the two ideas naturally and a little more softly than から.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: A frase encadeia uma causa e uma consequência usando ので ('porque/como'). A primeira parte 背がいたい ('as costas doem') é o motivo; a segunda 病院に行く ('vou ao hospital') é o resultado. O analisador separou ので em の + で, mas funciona como uma unidade só: a conjunção causal ので, que liga as duas ideias de forma natural e um pouco mais suave que から.

translation_literal.en: As for my back, it hurts, so, to the hospital I go.
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto às costas, dói, então, hospital ao vou.

translation.en: Since my back hurts, I'm going to the hospital.
translation.pt-BR: Como estou com dor nas costas, vou ao hospital.

conjugation_note.en: dictionary form of the い-adjective 痛い (いたい), affirmative present
conjugation_note.pt-BR: forma de dicionário do adjetivo-い 痛い (いたい), presente afirmativo

conjugation_note.en: dictionary form of 行く (affirmative present/future)
conjugation_note.pt-BR: forma de dicionário de 行く (presente/futuro afirmativo)

findings.issue: Generated JP 背がいたい is unnatural: for back pain natives say 背中が痛い (or 腰が痛い); bare 背 in modern usage reads as 'height/stature' (背が高い). If corrected, kana/romaji/token 背(せ) must be updated to 背中(せなか) as well.
findings.current: 背がいたいので病院に行く
findings.proposed: jp: 背中がいたいので病院に行く; kana: せなかがいたいのでびょういんにいく; romaji: senakagaitainodebyouinniiku; tokens[0]: s=背中, r=せなか (en 'back', pt 'costas' unchanged)

items.jp: 今日の講義はとても面白かった
items.kana: きょうのこうぎわとてもおもしろかった

structure_explanation.en: The subject-topic is 今日の講義 ('today's lecture'), where の links 今日 to 講義, and は marks it as the topic. とても ('very') is the adverb of degree. The predicate is 面白かった, the past of the い-adjective 面白い ('interesting'): 面白い → 面白かった. Note that the い-adjective carries the past on its own, without needing です.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: O sujeito-tópico é 今日の講義 ('a aula de hoje'), onde の liga 今日 a 講義, e は o marca como tópico. とても ('muito') é o advérbio de grau. O predicado é 面白かった, passado da い-adjetivo 面白い ('interessante'): 面白い → 面白かった. Repare que a い-adjetivo carrega sozinha o passado, sem precisar de です.

translation_literal.en: As for today's class, it was very interesting.
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto à aula de hoje, muito foi interessante.

translation.pt-BR: A aula de hoje foi muito interessante.

conjugation_note.en: past form of 面白い (い-adjective): 面白い → 面白かっ + た
conjugation_note.pt-BR: forma passada de 面白い (い-adjetivo): 面白い → 面白かっ + た

findings.issue: Gender error and terminology drift: 'da い-adjetivo' / 'a い-adjetivo' treat adjetivo as feminine; house style elsewhere (e.g. sent:gen-14cb4f2b3c7a) is 'o adjetivo-い'.
findings.current: passado da い-adjetivo 面白い ... Repare que a い-adjetivo carrega sozinha o passado
findings.proposed: passado do adjetivo-い 面白い ... Repare que o adjetivo-い carrega sozinho o passado

items.jp: 大きな鷲が山の上を翔る
items.kana: おおきなわしがやまのうえをかける

structure_explanation.en: Same motion structure: subject + が + traversed space + を + verb. 山の上 ('the top of the mountain') is formed from 山 + の + 上, and を marks that space as the path of the flight. 大きな is a 連体詞 that directly modifies 鷲 ('big eagle'). 翔る (かける) gives the sense of gliding through the air.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: Mesma estrutura de movimento: sujeito + が + lugar percorrido + を + verbo. 山の上 ('o topo/cima da montanha') é formado por 山 + の + 上, e を marca esse espaço como o trajeto do voo. 大きな é um 連体詞 que modifica diretamente 鷲 ('águia grande'). 翔る (かける) dá o tom de planar pelos ares.

translation_literal.en: A big eagle is flying (gliding) above the mountain.
translation_literal.pt-BR: Grande águia (que) o em-cima da montanha, voa (planando).

translation.en: A big eagle flies over the mountain.
translation.pt-BR: Uma águia grande voa por cima da montanha.

conjugation_note.en: dictionary (終止形) form of 翔る
conjugation_note.pt-BR: forma de dicionário (終止形) de 翔る

findings.issue: Generated JP tagged n5 uses 翔る (かける), a literary/poetic verb absent from any JLPT list, plus 鷲 (rare kanji). Grammatical but wildly implausible for N5; an N5 learner sentence would use 飛ぶ. Either reword or re-level.
findings.current: 大きな鷲が山の上を翔る
findings.proposed: Either re-level the sentence off n5, or reword jp to 大きな鳥が山の上を飛ぶ AND regenerate kana, romaji, en/pt, lit_*, expl_*, and tokens — they all reference 鷲 and 翔る.

findings.issue: Garbled literal mirror: '(que) o em-cima' is not parseable Portuguese and '(que)' does not render が; lit_en for the same sentence is clean. Needs rewording while keeping the structural mirror.
findings.current: Grande águia (que) o em-cima da montanha, voa (planando).
findings.proposed: Minimal fix preserving the literal-mirror style: 'Grande águia, o em-cima da montanha, voa (planando).' (just drop '(que)').

items.jp: この区には大きい公園があります
items.kana: このくにわおおきいこうえんがあります

structure_explanation.en: The sentence uses the existence structure 〜があります (something exists/there is). The place 区 (district) takes the particle に (of location) followed by は, forming には, which marks the place as the topic ("in this district, as for it..."). The い-adjective 大きい (big) comes before the noun 公園 (park) to describe it, and が marks what exists. The target here is the vocabulary 区 (administrative district).
structure_explanation.pt-BR: A frase usa a estrutura de existência 〜があります (algo existe/há). O lugar 区 (distrito) recebe a partícula に (de localização) seguida de は, formando には, que marca o lugar como tópico ("neste distrito, quanto a ele..."). O adjetivo い 大きい (grande) vem antes do substantivo 公園 (parque) para descrevê-lo, e が marca o que existe. O alvo aqui é o vocabulário 区 (distrito administrativo).

translation_literal.en: As for (in this district), there is a large park.
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto a (em este distrito), parque grande existe.

translation.en: There's a big park in this ward.
translation.pt-BR: Neste distrito tem um parque grande.

conjugation_note.en: dictionary form of the い-adjective 大きい
conjugation_note.pt-BR: forma de dicionário do adjetivo い 大きい

gloss.en: to exist, to be (for inanimate things)

conjugation_note.en: stem of ある in the polite form (ari- + ます)
conjugation_note.pt-BR: raiz de ある na forma polida (ari- + ます)

conjugation_note.en: auxiliary ます that makes the verb polite
conjugation_note.pt-BR: auxiliar ます que torna o verbo polido

findings.issue: Token この has role null, but この is a content word (adnominal), not a particle; the same word carries role 'adnominal (determinante)' in sent:gen-1bce6041e175. Inconsistent/missing data.

items.jp: 次の部屋に移りましょう
items.kana: つぎのへやにうつりましょう

structure_explanation.en: 次の部屋 ('the next room') uses の to link 次 (next) to 部屋 (room). The particle に marks the destination of the movement. The verb 移る ('to move, to pass to') appears in the form 〜ましょう (移りましょう), which is the polite volitional: an invitation/suggestion 'let's...'. The tone is polite.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: 次の部屋 ('a próxima sala') usa の para ligar 次 (próximo) a 部屋 (sala). A partícula に marca o destino do movimento. O verbo 移る ('mudar-se, passar para') aparece na forma 〜ましょう (移りましょう), que é o volitivo educado: um convite/sugestão 'vamos...'. O tom é polido.

translation_literal.en: To the next room, let's move.
translation_literal.pt-BR: Para a sala seguinte, vamos nos mudar.

translation.en: Let's move to the next room.

conjugation_note.en: ます form of 移る (stem 移り) linked to ましょう (polite volitional)
conjugation_note.pt-BR: forma ます de 移る (raiz 移り) ligada a ましょう (volitivo educado)

findings.issue: ましょう token has null gloss and null role, but it is a meaning-bearing auxiliary (polite volitional), not a particle; ます gets a gloss and role in other items of this batch. Missing data.
findings.proposed: Fix all three fields, not just en: en = "let's (do) (polite volitional)"; pt = "vamos (fazer) (volitivo polido)"; role = "auxiliar volitivo de polidez" — consistent with the ます tokens' 'auxiliar de polidez' pattern.
